The Friday Note · Issue #14

The Trust Premium

August 9, 2026 · Chris O'Hara

This week: Klaviyo's research lands a number that every marketer should internalize: 68% of consumers say AI-generated content feels less authentic. In an AI-saturated market, trust becomes the scarcest—and most valuable—asset.

📊 The Number

Authenticity Has a Price

68%
of consumers say AI-generated marketing
feels "less authentic"
Source: Klaviyo Consumer Research, 2026

This isn't a vague sentiment. It's a measurable perception gap—and it's growing. As AI-generated content floods every channel, consumers are developing detection instincts. They can't always articulate why something feels off, but they feel it.

The strategic implication is counterintuitive: the more AI content enters the market, the more valuable human-created content becomes. Not because humans write "better" in some abstract sense—but because authenticity itself is becoming scarce.

💡 The Framework

What Builds Trust When Everything Is Generated

If 68% of your audience is skeptical of AI content, how do you build trust? The answer isn't to pretend you're not using AI—it's to understand what trust signals actually work.

👤

Named Humans

Content attributed to a real person with a real track record. Not "the team at X" or worse, no attribution at all. A name, a face, a bio that can be verified.

📍

Specific Context

Details that couldn't be generated from generic training data. The name of the customer, the specific outcome, the nuance that only someone who was there would know.

⏱️

Timely Relevance

Content that responds to what's happening now—not evergreen filler that could have been written six months ago. Real-time signals that a human is paying attention.

🎯

Point of View

Opinions, arguments, takes that could be wrong. AI hedges; humans commit. The willingness to stake a position is itself a trust signal.

The paradox: AI can help you produce all of these things faster. But the moment they feel produced—rather than created—the trust evaporates.
📈 The Business Case

Trust Converts

This isn't just about warm feelings. The trust premium has measurable business outcomes:

Dentsu's B2B research found that a 10-point improvement in buyer experience—driven largely by trust and authenticity signals—correlates with a 14% uplift in opportunity value. Buyers pay more when they trust the vendor.

The Forrester data from Cannes showed that while 90% of agencies now use AI, creative effectiveness is declining. The efficiency gains are being offset by authenticity losses. More content, less impact.

And the Amazon Rufus data tells an interesting story: AI shopping assistants convert at 2-3x the rate of traditional search, but only when they can cite credible sources. The AI's persuasion power depends on the trust embedded in its references.

Trust isn't a soft metric anymore. It's a conversion rate, a deal size, a competitive moat. The companies that figure out how to build trust in an AI-saturated environment will outperform the ones that just optimize for volume.

🎯 What This Means

The Trust Premium Strategy

For content teams: Invest in bylines, expertise, and point of view. The generic "company blog" is losing credibility. Named authors with verifiable expertise are gaining it.

For product marketers: Customer stories matter more than ever—but only if they're specific and verifiable. Generic testimonials feel AI-generated even when they're not. Name the customer, quantify the outcome, include the detail that proves it's real.

For executives: Your personal brand is a trust asset. Showing up in public—on stage, in podcasts, on LinkedIn—signals that a human is behind the company. It's becoming a competitive advantage.

The irony is rich: the more AI can do, the more valuable humans become. Not because AI is bad at content—it's quite good. But because scarcity creates value, and authentic human judgment is becoming scarce.
